questions.question: Explain, with examples, why death can happen at any stage of a life cycle.
questions.expected_answer: Living things face many dangers at every stage. Eggs can be eaten by predators like honey badgers or washed away, young animals can be eaten or starve, seedlings can dry out or be eaten, and adults can die from disease, drought, fire, predators or people. Not every living thing reaches old age.

questions.question: Why do sea turtles, fish and frogs produce so many young?
questions.expected_answer: They give no care, so most of their young die from predators and other dangers. Because so many are produced, a few survive to become adults and reproduce, which keeps the life cycle going.

questions.question: Give two examples of animals that care for their young, and describe how they do it.
questions.expected_answer: African penguins take turns to keep their eggs warm and bring food for the chicks. Elephant mothers feed calves milk, and the herd protects them. Nile crocodile mothers guard the nest and carry the babies to the water in their mouths. People care for children for many years.
